correctness.rationale: The proof imports the exact finite-count theorem from arXiv:2610.02018v1, then uses a coefficientwise refinement inequality. Any finite discriminant datum must have a Jordan block of size at least two, because the all-size-one repeated-eigenvalue case is diagonalizable and infinite. Refining all blocks while retaining one size-two block gives (2,1^{n-2}), whose coefficient is the claimed bound. The explicit symmetric nilpotent 2x2 block squared to zero and direct sum with distinct scalars realizes equality. Pascal's identity gives the exact gap. The checker independently replays the symbolic identities and partition stress tests.

value.rationale: The result quantifies the sharp finite failure mode exactly on the newly identified ED discriminant. It gives a forbidden finite interval below the generic ED degree and an exact minimal finite drop, valid uniformly for all n and k. The sharp witness shows that the smallest defective Jordan block already realizes the worst finite degeneration, while real discriminant data behave qualitatively differently by having infinite critical sets. This is a natural global complexity boundary rather than a routine numerical specialization.
